close_reason: opinion: tuple vs separate let bindings is style, not engineering
description: Lines 1202-1211: 'let (mut nc_permitted, mut nc_excluded) = match &anchor.name_constraints { None => (None, default), Some(nc) => (...) }' bundles two semantically independent initializations into one tuple match. A reader must mentally unpair both fields simultaneously to understand each. Separate bindings make the intent clear: 'let mut nc_permitted = anchor.name_constraints.as_ref().and_then(|nc| nc.permitted_subtrees.clone()); let mut nc_excluded = anchor.name_constraints.as_ref().and_then(|nc| nc.excluded_subtrees.clone()).unwrap_or_default();'
title: NC seeding: split tuple destructuring into separate let bindings
